name: Adobe Fonts
description: Adobe Fonts is a Creative Cloud type library for browsing and activating font families and variations, managing desktop fonts, and publishing licensed web fonts through Adobe-hosted web projects and embed code.
agentUseSummary: Adobe's only documented automation surface is the legacy Typekit v1 API, which uses user-generated static tokens, old Typekit hosts and kit terminology, and has no delegated authorization flow. Relay mounts no connection or font/kit tools until Adobe confirms the API's current support and licensing contract and a bounded read-only resource is selected.

blocked.label: Change Adobe Fonts
blocked.description: Kit or web-project creation, modification, publication, font activation, embedding, downloading, and all mutations are unavailable.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No font or kit action can be enabled until the legacy API, authentication, and licensing contract are reviewed.

providerSetup.blocker: The documented API still presents itself as Typekit API v1, uses typekit.com endpoints and user-generated X-Typekit-Token credentials, and says delegated authentication is a future feature, while current Adobe Fonts licensing requires Adobe-hosted web-font embed code and prohibits self-hosting.
providerSetup.nextAction: Obtain Adobe confirmation that the Typekit v1 API remains supported for new Adobe Fonts integrations, document token issuance/rotation/revocation and commercial rate limits, confirm permitted metadata and web-project automation under current licensing, and select a bounded read-only family or kit metadata surface before implementing encrypted customer token storage.

evidence.supports: Adobe hosts documentation for a Typekit REST API that can read font metadata and create, modify, and publish kits, but the surface retains legacy Typekit identity and terminology.
The documented API uses user-generated static X-Typekit-Token credentials and states delegated authentication is planned for the future rather than currently supported.
The documented v1 API is rooted at typekit.com and includes GET reads plus POST and DELETE kit mutations.
Adobe states web fonts must be used through Adobe-provided embed code and current terms do not allow self-hosting or uploading font files to a website platform.
Adobe describes the current product as a Creative Cloud subscription service for browsing, activating, managing, and using fonts on desktop and web.
